arguments.text:
CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE (read from astropy/timeseries/core.py v1, lines ~57-84, `BaseTimeSeries._check_required_columns`):

```
plural = 's' if len(required_columns) > 1 else ''
if not relax and len(self.colnames) == 0:
    raise ValueError("... expected '{}' as the first column{} but time series has no columns".format(cls, required_columns[0], plural))
elif self.colnames[:len(required_columns)] != required_columns:
    raise ValueError("... expected '{}' as the first column{} but found '{}'".format(cls, required_columns[0], plural, self.colnames[0]))
```

The *test* is on the full prefix list, but the *message* only names required_columns[0] and colnames[0].
So when _required_columns=['time','flux'] and 'flux' is removed: colnames=['time'], prefix ['time'] != ['time','flux'] -> correct detection, but message says "expected 'time' as the first columns but found 'time'". Self-contradictory. Exactly the issue report.

FIX SHAPE I'd accept in review:
1. Keep existing zero-column branch behaviour (message unchanged is fine/acceptable).
2. In the elif branch: if the leading columns still match required_columns[0] (i.e. condition fails due to trailing missing required columns), raise a message that names the MISSING required columns, e.g. "TimeSeries object is invalid - missing required column(s) 'flux'". Only keep the "expected '<first>' as the first column(s) but found '<col>'" wording when colnames[0] genuinely != required_columns[0].
3. Must not regress: _required_columns_relax behaviour, multi-column required, QTable/TimeSeries subclasses (BinnedTimeSeries etc.), and the existing test asserting "'TimeSeries object is invalid'" at astropy/timeseries/tests/test_common.py:61.

WATCH: `plural = 's' if len(required_columns) > 1` — with relax the slice length differs; a naive rewrite that changes `required_columns` also changes `plural` and can alter messages in the relax path. Keep relax semantics identical.
